q: The intensity of a wave is the power or energy per unit time transported per unit ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The intensity of a wave is the power or energy per unit time transported per unit cross-sectional area.

q: The intensity of a wave is calculated using the formula ____.
e: The intensity of a wave is calculated using the formula I = (P)/(A). Leave the relation as I = (P)/(A).

q: In the intensity formula, $P$ represents the ____ of the wave.
e: In the intensity formula, P represents the power of the wave. Power is what this statement is using.

q: In SI units, the unit of intensity of a wave is ____.
e: In SI units, the unit of intensity of a wave is W m^-2. The unit written here is W m^-2.

q: By considering the source of sound as a point source, the sound wave can be distributed uniformly over a spherical wave front of area ____.
e: By considering the source of sound as a point source, the sound wave can be distributed uniformly over a spherical wave front of area 4π r². Leave the relation as 4π r².

q: Hence, the wave intensity at a distance $r$ from a point source is ____.
e: Hence, the wave intensity at a distance r from a point source is I = (P)/(4π r²). Leave the relation as I = (P)/(4π r²).

q: For a particular source, intensity varies ____ with the square of the distance from the source.
e: For a particular source, intensity varies inversely with the square of the distance from the source. Inversely is what this statement is using.

q: Intensity of a wave obeys the ____ law.
e: Intensity of a wave obeys the inverse square law. Inverse square is what this statement is using.

q: The intensity of a wave is directly proportional to the ____ of the amplitude of the wave.
e: The intensity of a wave is directly proportional to the square of the amplitude of the wave. Square is what this statement is using.
